variables.rooms: {% set ns = namespace(l=[]) %}{% for b in states.input_boolean | selectattr('entity_id', 'match', '^input_boolean\.sleeping_') | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') %}{% set a = area_id(b.entity_id) %}{% set occ = ((area_entities(a) | select('match', '^binary_sensor\.magic_areas_presence_tracking_.+_area_state$') | select('is_state', 'on') | list | count) > 0) if a else false %}{% set ns.l = ns.l + [[b.entity_id, occ]] %}{% endfor %}{{ ns.l }}

variables.clear: {% if window_ok %}{% set ns = namespace(l=[]) %}{% for r in rooms %}{% if not r[1] %}{% set ns.l = ns.l + [r[0]] %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{{ ns.l }}{% else %}{{ [] }}{% endif %}

description: 2026-11-27 (operator): 'Sleeping here' (input_boolean.sleeping_<room>) marks a room where someone is asleep; the climate loop keeps its AC from blowing air there and presence lighting is paused. A toggle clears itself between 12:00 and 20:00 once its room is EMPTY (its Magic Areas presence state is off), so a forgotten toggle cannot leave a room unheated for days. Review #71: a plain 12:00 clear re-ran the climate loop and could start the AC on a guest still asleep, so an occupied room keeps its toggle until it empties. Outside the window an empty-looking room never clears it: a sleeper lying still can read empty. Rooms with no presence sensor read empty and clear at 12:00. Tests: tests/climate/cases.py (sleeping clear). Design: docs/climate-control-design.md, v6.2.
